clue.text: Land alternative for this vehicle to work on

parts.note: a tract is a stretch of land
or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a farm vehicle as the best machine for working the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer's tractor is the motor machine used for ploughing and hauling in the fields.

clue.text: Realism? Means-test odd clothing items

indicators.note: odd here asks for the letters in the odd-numbered places, first, third, fifth and so on, across the two words

explanation.surface: A puzzled comment on a benefits means-test, followed by some strange garments.
explanation.walkthrough: Run 'Realism' and 'Means-test' together and take every odd letter: R, A, I, M, E, N, T, S. 'Odd' seems to describe the clothing but is the selection signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old word for garments, so its plural names pieces of dress.

clue.text: Clone me a breed of lizard

indicators.note: to breed is to produce something new, so these letters are reworked into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A request to a geneticist to clone the speaker into a new kind of reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breed' rearranges CLONEMEA. CAMELEON is a less common spelling of chameleon.
explanation.definitionFit: The chameleon, here in a variant spelling, is a colour-changing reptile of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Extreme way to leave the trenches

explanation.definitionFit: Going beyond reason is excessive; in the First World War soldiers climbed out of their trench and over its parapet to attack.

clue.text: Touched by a material thing

explanation.surface: Something was handled by a fabric object.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sensed by contact is the past tense of feel; the matted wool fabric is also called by the same name.

clue.text: Sour beer or a lager perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders whether the bitter brew is beer or a lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ALAGER. Alegar is malt vinegar, literally soured ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Alegar is vinegar brewed from ale that has gone acid, so a soured malt drink.

clue.text: First course, for Stratford players in box office hit, lacks original ingredients

indicators.note: in places the theatre company inside the other letters
lacks says a letter is taken away from the word hit

parts.note: a hit is a popular success, kept here as written

indicators.note: original asks for the opening letter of ingredients

parts.note: the RSC, the Royal Shakespeare Company, is based at Stratford-upon-Avon

explanation.surface: A theatre review complains that a Shakespeare company's hit show lacks its original ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks original ingredients' takes I (the first letter of 'ingredients') from HIT, leaving HT; BO + HT is opened by RSC, Britain's Royal Shakespeare Company at Stratford.
explanation.definitionFit: Borscht, the beetroot soup, is served as a starter, the opening dish of a meal.

clue.text: Colonize around a place in, say, Washington

indicators.note: around says the word for colonize goes about the letter A

parts.note: to settle a land is to colonize it

explanation.surface: Settlers colonize the land around a spot in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the biggest city in the state of Washington, an example of a place there.

clue.text: Go for it in unrestrained fashion

definitions.text: Go for it in unrestrained fashion

parts.words: Go for it in unrestrained fashion
parts.note: describes giving free rein, releasing something or oneself without restraint

explanation.definitionFit: To release or unleash means acting freely with no restraint.

clue.text: Motion picture regulated by the cinema scenery…

parts.note: a film is a motion picture
set, as in adjusted, means regulated

explanation.surface: A movie made to the rules of the cinema backdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: The constructed backdrop where a movie is shot is the studio scenery for the cinema.

clue.text: … And theatre ready for expectation of something to come?

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession
set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go'

explanation.surface: Following the film clue, the theatre is prepared and waiting for what happens next.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue about cinema scenery; 'And' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: When the stage is set, everything is arranged in anticipation of an event about to happen.

clue.text: Even with scores in a mess, obtain the outline plans

indicators.note: a mess is a muddle, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A coach tries to get a game plan from scores in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' rearranges SCORESINA; 'Even with', 'obtain' and 'the' are padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenarios are sketched-out sequences of events, a plot or plan in summary.

clue.text: Book concludes the strong feeling of a fanatic

indicators.note: concludes says the book abbreviation comes at the end

parts.note: zeal is fervour, a strong feeling
OT is the Old Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A book ends with a fanatic's passionate conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is an extremist devotee of a cause.

clue.text: According to ranking, hire, we hear, shrewd man

indicators.note: we hear says the word hire is spoken rather than written

parts.note: the word hire, said out loud
arch means knowing or sly, so shrewd
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: An employer hires a clever chap, going by the rank list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns HIRE into HIER by sound. HIERARCHAL is a variant of hierarchical.
explanation.definitionFit: Hierarchal describes a graded order of ranks, from top to bottom.

clue.text: Et, for instance, has a note on disaffection

parts.note: ET, the film extraterrestrial, is an example of an alien
ti is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the Latin word 'et' sits next to a note in a disaffected text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Et' looks like the Latin 'and' but is ET, the film's extraterrestrial.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienation is estrangement, a feeling of being cut off or hostile.

clue.text: Bergamot toilet water produces some essential oil

indicators.note: some of says just part of the letters running across Bergamot toilet is taken

explanation.surface: Bergamot-scented eau de toilette yields some of its aromatic oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'bergamOT TOilet'. Otto, also attar, is rose oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is attar, the fragrant volatile extract distilled from rose petals.

clue.text: Taint iron chemically by treatment with acid

indicators.note: chemically suggests a reaction that changes the arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Iron is tainted by a chemical reaction when treated with acid.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitration is the reaction introducing a nitro group, usually using nitric acid.

clue.text: Deny that over four are not positive

indicators.note: over says the word for deny covers the Roman numeral, wrapping round it

parts.note: to negate is to deny
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone disputes that more than four people are pessimistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means covering: the word for deny lies over the numeral, enclosing it, not 'more than' as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A negative number or answer is one that is the opposite of a positive one.

clue.text: Cryptic clues to a meeting of the lips

definitions.note: a noun phrase defining a verb: to kiss is to make the lips meet

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or disguised, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A crossword setter's tricky clues lead up to a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' rearranges CLUESTOA. The definition is a noun phrase for a verb meaning to kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is the formal word for to kiss.

clue.text: To outshine at the back of the theatre

definitions.text: at the back of the theatre

explanation.surface: An actor steals the scene at the rear of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw attention from others is to overshadow; on stage, the area furthest from the audience is the rear.

clue.text: Meddle about with the unrefined manners of Mrs Grundy

indicators.note: about says the word for meddle surrounds the word for unrefined

parts.note: to pry is to meddle nosily
rude, in the sense of crude or coarse

explanation.surface: A busybody fusses about the coarse behaviour of a strait-laced woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Grundy, from an 18th-century play, is a British byword for a narrow-minded, prim moraliser.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudery is excessive concern with propriety, the hallmark of a prim moraliser.

clue.text: Tranquil midshipman

explanation.definitionFit: Easy means relaxed and calm; Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Captain Marryat's 1836 naval novel.

clue.text: Understanding 'the knowledge'

explanation.definitionFit: Perception is insight or comprehension, and also awareness gained through the senses.

clue.text: Declare some of the French left having eaten one cake

indicators.note: having eaten says the hidden letters take in the numeral for one
some of asks for a run of letters from inside the word Declare

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone announces that some of the French have gone after eating a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair is a finger of choux pastry filled with cream, a small cake.

clue.text: A graduate begins calculus on university's calculator

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: begins asks for just the opening letter of calculus

parts.note: U for university, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A graduate starts learning calculus with the college's calculating device.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a counting frame of beads on rods, an early computing tool.

clue.text: Are kids those who saunter?

explanation.definitionFit: Toddlers are small children learning to walk; to toddle also means to stroll casually.

clue.text: Plunder the castle

explanation.surface: Raid the fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook is to swindle or fleece; in chess the castle is another name for the same piece.

clue.text: Smallest dress size mother left behind

indicators.note: behind says the abbreviation for left comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a mini is a very short dress length
ma is a familiar name for mother

explanation.surface: Mum leaves behind the smallest size of dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Minimal means least possible, the barest amount.

clue.text: Soaring right over a fortified location for troops

indicators.note: over, as in turned over, suggests these letters are upset into a new order

explanation.surface: An aircraft soaring right over a military fort.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is a fortified post or town where soldiers are stationed.

clue.text: Desmond, looking back, never accepted being ridiculed

indicators.note: accepted says the reversed name takes in the word for never
looking back says the short form of Desmond is read backwards

parts.note: Des is the short form of Desmond
ne'er is a poetic contraction of never

explanation.surface: Desmond glances back and never accepts the mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' makes SED from the short form of Desmond; 'accepted' has it take in the poetic contraction of never.
explanation.definitionFit: To sneer is to mock or scoff with contempt.
